hypothesis: Local-Sum QNN adds incremental predictive value to XGBoost
architecture: XGBoost + Local-Sum-QNN (OOF stacked) vs XGBoost alone
reason_rejected: CI crosses zero -- not statistically distinguishable from noise on 250 CONFIRM_VAL rows.
what_was_learned: Even a real, statistically-confirmed quantum-architecture-level improvement (Local-Sum beating Global QNN) does not automatically translate into a system-level predictive contribution once a strong classical model (XGBoost) is already in the ensemble.

hypothesis: Local-Sum QNN's contribution to XGBoost is specifically quantum, not just 'another nonlinear feature'
architecture: XGBoost + Local-Sum-QNN vs XGBoost + classical MLP capacity control (same 1-D output, same reduced features)
result: PR-AUC 0.9665 vs 0.9671 -- the CLASSICAL control is marginally HIGHER. Delta -0.0007, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0072,+0.0057], crosses zero.
reason_rejected: This is the decisive negative result of the round: even setting aside statistical significance, the point estimate favors the classical control, not the quantum component. A same-capacity classical nonlinear feature does at least as well as the quantum feature in this ensemble.
what_was_learned: The classical-capacity-control methodology worked exactly as intended -- it caught what would otherwise have looked like a positive result (XGBoost+Local-Sum beats XGBoost alone by a small margin) and correctly reframed it as 'any nonlinear feature would likely do the same or better', not 'quantum helped'.

hypothesis: Recall/F1/F2 improve alongside PR-AUC for Local-Sum QNN
architecture: Fixed 0.5-threshold classification metrics, 20 seeds, Local-Sum vs Global
result: Delta Recall -0.0853 (CI excludes zero, negative), Delta F1 -0.0452, Delta F2 -0.0741 -- all worse for Local-Sum despite PR-AUC and Precision improving.
reason_rejected: Most plausibly a threshold-calibration artifact (the two observables have different natural output scales), not evidence against the PR-AUC finding -- but a genuine, disclosed complication that a system relying on threshold-based decisions (not pure ranking) would need to resolve via per-model threshold tuning before Local-Sum could be used as-is.
what_was_learned: PR-AUC improvements do not automatically imply improvements on every threshold-dependent operational metric -- a properly matched operating-point comparison (recall at matched precision) is needed before claiming Local-Sum is unambiguously better for a deployed decision rule, not just a better ranker.
